bottomLine: Two HM Treasury consultations now set concrete response dates for payments and digital settlement services, while EIOPA's Solvency II package, FINMA's quantum guidance and the financial-services AI plan create implementation and governance work.

horizon.title: Response deadline: Bank of England fee regime for recognised payment systems

prompts.owner: Who owns the response on payment-system and digital-settlement supervisory fees?
prompts.action: Assess scope, fee-cap impacts and whether to submit evidence before 31 August.
prompts.evidence: Documented response decision, impact assessment and approved submission where relevant.

horizon.title: Response deadline: Modernising Payment Services Regulation

prompts.owner: Who owns the response across payments, Open Banking, tokenisation and agentic payments?
prompts.action: Map proposed reforms to products, customer protections and operating-model dependencies.
prompts.evidence: Committee-approved response position and traceable product and control impact assessment.

horizon.title: Revised Solvency II framework begins to apply

prompts.owner: Who owns Solvency II implementation across liquidity, risk margin, matching adjustment and reporting?
prompts.action: Confirm applicability, implementation milestones and dependencies before the revised framework applies.
prompts.evidence: Approved implementation plan, accountable owners, gap assessment and reporting change log.

signals.title: Updating the Bank of England’s fee regime for recognised payment systems
signals.why: HM Treasury is consulting on extending the Bank's supervisory fee regime to digital settlement asset service providers and on the level of fee caps; responses close on 31 August 2026.

signals.title: EIOPA completes Solvency II Review mandate with final guidelines and draft technical standards
signals.why: EIOPA completed its Solvency II Review package, including liquidity-risk guidance and technical standards affecting risk margin, matching adjustment and reporting; the revised framework applies from 30 January 2027.

signals.title: FINMA guidance on quantum computing
signals.why: FINMA calls for forward-looking quantum-risk planning, including migration roadmaps, cryptographic inventories, protection against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks and external-provider involvement.

signals.title: Modernising Payment Services Regulation
signals.why: HM Treasury is seeking views on updating payment-services regulation for tokenised payments, Open Banking and agentic payments while maintaining consumer protections; responses close on 6 October 2026.

signals.title: AI Adoption Plan: Financial Services
signals.why: The independent plan makes ten recommendations spanning the regulatory framework, AI-enabled advice, resilience, skills and agentic payments; the government has accepted its recommendations for government.

warnings.message: This reviewed edition contains material rows from three primary authorities. Quiet themes remain watch-listed because the wider source universe did not report cleanly enough to support a whole-market conclusion.
HM Treasury supplies three of five material signals. Treat the bottom line as concentrated UK policy evidence rather than a complete cross-market view.
